title: Heat transfer problem of a dense gas described by the Enskog equation with a modification of the Enskog factor
authors: Shigeru Takata, Soma Sakata, Masanari Hattori
abstract: Heat transfer in a dense gas between two parallel plates is studied for assessing the quantitative difference of two variants of the Enskog equation, i.e., the original Enskog equation and the Enskog equation with a modified Enskog factor recently proposed in Phys. Rev. E \textbf{111}, 065108 (2025). The main advantage of the latter is that the H theorem, which is lacking in the former, has been established. The influence of the modification is assessed by comparing the macroscopic quantities in details. It is found that the influence of this modification is quite limited in the density, temperature, and heat flow vector. However, the influence on the stress tensor is visible in some severe setting of parameters.
summary: This paper investigates heat transfer in a dense gas by comparing the standard Enskog equation with a modified version that includes a new factor. Numerical simulations show that while the modification has little effect on bulk properties like temperature, it causes a measurable difference in the stress tensor, especially under high confinement. This highlights the importance of subtle theoretical modifications in accurately modeling non-equilibrium transport phenomena.
main_problem: The study compares the heat transfer in a dense gas using two variants of the Enskog equation: the original and a modified version incorporating a new factor.
main_result: The modification has a limited influence on temperature, density, and heat flow, but a visible difference appears in the stress tensor, particularly in highly confined gas regimes.
method: The authors performed a numerical study of the time-dependent heat transfer problem by solving the kinetic equation using finite-difference and spectral methods.
model_or_system: The system is a dense gas confined between two parallel plates, modeled using the Enskog equation framework for hard spheres.
key_observables: Temperature (T), density (rho), heat flow vector (q_1), and the stress tensor (p_ij).
important_parameters: Confinement ratio (sigma/L), Knudsen number (Kn), and the ratio of boundary temperatures (T_+/T_-).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes hard spheres, uses the Carnahan–Starling EoS, and considers one-dimensional behavior in the transverse directions.
figures_summary: Figures show the time evolution of T and q_1 agreeing between models, while p_11 shows divergence, especially in confined cases. Other figures quantify this difference's dependence on Kn and confinement.
paper_structure: The paper sets up the heat transfer problem, compares the OEE and EESM formulations, numerically solves the resulting kinetic equations, and analyzes the resulting macroscopic quantities, focusing on the differences in the stress tensor.
why_interesting: While focused on classical gas dynamics, the rigorous comparison of kinetic equations and the establishment of theorems (like H theorem) are fundamental techniques applicable to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics problems in quantum systems.
